entries.description_source_en: Much remains unknown about this Pokémon, as few have ever seen it. However, we know that it is calm and dislikes conflict, and it enjoys polishing its face against trees and rocks.
entries.fact_source_en: This Pokémon lived in primeval jungles. Few enemies would have been willing to square off against its heavily armored face, so it’s thought.

entries.description_source_en: Its face is sturdy—as strong as diamond—and this hardness offers a very stable defense. Much about this species is still unknown, such as its natural habitat.
entries.fact_source_en: It lived in the same environments as Rampardos. Their fossils have been found together— seemingly from after they’d fought to the finish.

entries.description_source_en: If its cloak is even slightly damaged, Burmy will immediately repair it with whatever is close at hand. The Pokémon within the cloak is scrawny and vulnerable to the cold.
entries.fact_source_en: To shelter itself from cold, wintry winds, it covers itself with a cloak made of twigs and leaves.

entries.description_source_en: When Burmy evolved, its cloak became a part of this Pokémon’s body. The cloak is never shed.
entries.fact_source_en: Its appearance changes depending on where it evolved. The materials on hand become a part of its body.

entries.description_source_en: Scatters steel-colored scales as it flaps its wings. Despite being observed feeding primarily on the nectar of flowers, Mothim is not often seen around flower gardens.
entries.fact_source_en: While it loves floral honey, it won’t gather any itself. Instead, it plots to steal some from COMBEE.

entries.description_source_en: They swear fealty to a queen Pokémon and work diligently to gather nectar. Each swarm produces a different flavor of honey.
entries.fact_source_en: The members of the trio spend all their time together. Each one has a slightly different taste in nectar.

entries.description_source_en: Commands its subjects to build its hive. It will dispatch any interlopers who dare sneak into its nest and use them as nourishment for itself.
entries.fact_source_en: It skillfully commands its grubs in battles with its enemies. The grubs are willing to risk their lives to defend Vespiquen.

entries.description_source_en: A species related to the Pikachu line. Though Pachirisu is a calm Pokémon, it still presents a danger should one touch its electrified tail or cheeks.
entries.fact_source_en: It makes electricity with pouches in its cheeks and shoots charges from its tail. It lives atop trees.

entries.description_source_en: It moves freely in the water by spinning its forked tail for propulsion. The resemblance to the screw of a steamboat is coincidental.
entries.fact_source_en: It spins its two tails like a screw to propel itself through water. The tails also slice clinging seaweed.

entries.description_source_en: Has a long, rather splendid flotation sac, which prevents Floatzel from drowning even in stormy seas. One might glimpse this species around fishing hamlets from time to time.
entries.fact_source_en: With its flotation sac inflated, it can carry people on its back. It deflates the sac before it dives.

entries.description_source_en: Once the fruit growing alongside the main body is large and plump, Cherubi will use the nutrients within to evolve. The fruit then detaches, becoming nourishment for other creatures.
entries.fact_source_en: It nimbly dashes about to avoid getting pecked by bird Pokémon that would love to make off with its small, nutrient-rich storage ball.

entries.description_source_en: Motionless, save for the occasional quiver. A rich array of Pokémon can be found gathered around it, drawn by the scent exuded from Cherrim's folded petals.
entries.fact_source_en: Its folded petals are pretty tough. Bird Pokémon can peck at them all they want, and Cherrim won’t be bothered at all.

entries.description_source_en: Found in abundance on seashores bordering warm waters. Shellos are unexpectedly friendly and will crawl toward any person they see. Take care not to get coated in mucus!
entries.fact_source_en: For the most part, it makes its home along the seashore. Its color and form differ according to its habitat and the quality of its food.

entries.description_source_en: Eats beach sand for nourishment. Should one Gastrodon encounter another of a different color, a fierce battle will inevitably ensue.
entries.fact_source_en: The softness of its body helps disperse the force of impacts, so although its body is uncommonly squishy, it’s also surprisingly resilient.

entries.description_source_en: To affirm their kinship, members of this species will form a ring by linking their newly doubled tails together. On rare occasions, humans have been accepted into such rings.
entries.fact_source_en: It uses its tails for everything. If it wraps both of its tails around you and gives you a squeeze, that’s proof it really likes you.

entries.description_source_en: Said to lure away young children and carry them off to the afterlife. Some whisper that Drifloon are formed of reincarnated human souls, but these rumors are as yet unconfirmed.
entries.fact_source_en: Perhaps seeking company, it approaches children. However, it often quickly runs away again when the children play too roughly with it.

entries.description_source_en: It drifts along at dusk, perfectly silent. Its transient, melancholy aspect touches some people deeply—every so often, one will come upon a song or poem devoted to Drifblim.
entries.fact_source_en: The raw material for the gas inside its body is souls. When its body starts to deflate, it’s thought to carry away people and Pokémon.

entries.description_source_en: My hypothesis as to why Buneary rolls up its ears is that its hearing is far too keen. I surmise that the Pokémon protects its hearing by limiting the sound that may enter its ears.
entries.fact_source_en: Buneary can attack by rolling up their ears and then striking with the force created by unrolling them. This attack becomes stronger with training.

entries.description_source_en: Its fur is warm and yet remarkably light. This Pokémon kicks as though it were a master of karate, driving back its opponents with ease.
entries.fact_source_en: Once hot seasons are over, Lopunny’s coat will be replaced with fur that holds a lot of insulating air in preparation for colder weather.

entries.description_source_en: The incantations Mismagius chants can ward against misfortune, so a custom exists of inviting it into one's home. Incur the Pokémon's displeasure, however, and disaster will surely ensue.
entries.fact_source_en: Mismagius have been known to cast spells to make people fall in love, so some people search for this Pokémon as if their life depended on it.

entries.description_source_en: One cry from this Pokémon, and a murder of Murkrow come flying. At such times, one would think the curtain of night had fallen, plunging the world into jet-black darkness.
entries.fact_source_en: Its goons take care of most of the fighting for it. The only time it dirties its own hands is in delivering a final blow to finish off an opponent.

entries.description_source_en: Bewitches humans with its helical tail and piercing gaze. Its hidden claws are quite sharp as well, making this Pokémon an exceedingly tricky opponent if antagonized.
entries.fact_source_en: It hides its spiteful tendency of hooking its claws into the nose of its Trainer if it isn’t fed.

entries.description_source_en: Though impudent and difficult to tame, Purugly enjoys great popularity due to its fur, the beauty of which surpasses even velveteen.
entries.fact_source_en: It binds its body with its tails to make itself look bigger. If it locks eyes, it will glare ceaselessly.

entries.description_source_en: This Pokémon gave me an excruciating headache when it seemingly cried out without making a sound. Perhaps there are some sounds that the human ear is simply incapable of hearing.
entries.fact_source_en: It emits high-frequency cries that people can’t hear. Once it starts, it can cry for an awfully long time.

entries.description_source_en: The poison that gushes from its aft end is accompanied by an utterly evil-smelling odor with such potency that one whiff can induce memory loss.
entries.fact_source_en: From its rear, it sprays a foul-smelling liquid at opponents. It aims for their faces, and it can hit them from over 16 feet away.
